spec.notes: Long names with improving news sentiment.

claim.text: Research-period backtest: Sharpe 2.2, annual return 11%, maximum drawdown 4%.

exhibits.summary: Delaying the signal by 1 more bar moves the Sharpe ratio from 2.22 to 2.18 (change -0.03).
Under strict point-in-time data the Sharpe ratio moves from 2.22 to 2.22. Strict mode changed no field or operator the signal uses.
At 10 bps the Sharpe ratio is 2.15 (as submitted, 8 bps: 2.22); it breaks even at 72.1 bps with daily turnover 0.07.
On the full universe the Sharpe ratio is 2.22 against 2.22 as submitted; the strategy never saw 0 delisted assets.
On the sealed period (strict mode, 10 bps) the Sharpe ratio is 0.37 against 2.22 in research, a gap of +1.85.
The best year gives 71% of total P&L (year 1) and calm regimes give 54%; Sharpe is 1.61 in calm and 5.91 in stressed regimes.
The log holds 4 distinct specs; the best of 4 under no edge is expected to reach a Sharpe of 0.42, so the claimed 2.20 becomes 1.78 and the probability that the true Sharpe is above zero is 98%.
The real signal's gross Sharpe of 2.50 beats 100% of 200 shuffled signals (shuffled mean -0.02, 95th percentile 1.20).
Perturbing the 1 numeric value in the signal by up to 50% moves the Sharpe ratio from 2.22 to as low as 1.31 (as low as 1.31 at 25%).
The top 1% of days (4 days) give 37% of total P&L and the top 5 assets give 44% (net of the strategy's own costs).

series.label: cumulative share of P&L, best days first
